book.title: The Starless Sea
book.description: NATIONAL BESTSELLER • From the bestselling author of The Night Circus, a timeless love story set in a secret underground world—a place of pirates, painters, lovers, liars, and ships that sail upon a starless sea. Zachary Ezra Rawlins is a graduate student in Vermont when he discovers a mysterious book hidden in the stacks. As he turns the pages, entranced by tales of lovelorn prisoners, key collectors, and nameless acolytes, he reads something strange: a story from his own childhood. Bewildered by this inexplicable book and desperate to make sense of how his own life came to be recorded, Zachary uncovers a series of clues—a bee, a key, and a sword—that lead him to a masquerade party in New York, to a secret club, and through a doorway to an ancient library hidden far below the surface of the earth. What Zachary finds in this curious place is more than just a buried home for books and their guardians—it is a place of lost cities and seas, lovers who pass notes under doors and across time, and of stories whispered by the dead. Zachary learns of those who have sacrificed much to protect this realm, relinquishing their sight and their tongues to preserve this archive, and also of those who are intent on its destruction. Together with Mirabel, a fierce, pink-haired protector of the place, and Dorian, a handsome, barefoot man with shifting alliances, Zachary travels the twisting tunnels, darkened stairwells, crowded ballrooms, and sweetly soaked shores of this magical world, discovering his purpose—in both the mysterious book and in his own life.

book.description: A masterwork by the incomparable, genre-defying, wondrous Italo Calvino. You go into a bookshop and buy If on a Winter's Night a Traveller by Italo Calvino. You like it. But there is a printer's error in your copy. You take it back to the shop and get a replacement. But the replacement seems to be a totally different story. You try to track down the original book you were reading but end up with a different narrative again. This remarkable novel leads you through many different books including a detective adventure, a romance, a satire, an erotic story, a diary and a quest. catalogueCheck.title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveller
catalogueCheck.description:
A novel built from beginnings...

You buy a book called If on a Winter’s Night a Traveller and sit down to read. The story stops mid-sentence. When you find another copy, it contains a different opening. Each attempt to continue leads to a new narrative that breaks off just as it gathers momentum.

As the Reader, you set out to track down the missing text. Along the way you encounter Ludmilla, another reader pursuing the same vanished book. What follows is a sequence of interrupted stories: thrillers, romances, political intrigues, each complete in its promise but not in its conclusion.

This novel turns reading itself into the central drama. The search for the next chapter becomes the plot. Every ending leads back to another beginning.

'Breathtakingly inventive' David Mitchell

'A writer of dizzying ambition and variety, each of his stories is a fresh adventure into the possibilities of fiction' Guardian

book.title: Moonflower Murders
book.description: From New York Times-bestselling author Anthony Horowitz comes a new novel featuring ex-editor hero Susan Ryeland, set to solve another murder mystery Farlingaye Hall is a beautiful hotel in Suffolk on the east coast of England. Unfortunately, it is also the site of the brutal murder of Frank Parris, a retired advertising executive. Stefan Codrescu, a Romanian maintenance man, is arrested after police discover blood spatter on his clothes and bed linen. He is found guilty and sentenced to eight years in prison. It appears to be an open-and-shut case, but there is more to it than meets the eye. Alan Conway, the late author of the fictional Magpie Murders, knew Frank Parris and once visited Farlingaye Hall. Also, the third book in Conway's detective series, Atticus Pund Takes the Cake, was based on the hotel. Cecily Treherne, the daughter of Farlingaye Hall's owner, has read the book and believes the proof of Stefan's innocence can be found in its pages. But now . . . Cecily Treherne has disappeared. So Conway's former editor, Susan Ryeland, leaves her own hotel in Crete and travels to Suffolk to investigate the murder and Treherne's disappearance. Masterfully intriguing, brilliantly clever and relentlessly suspenseful, Moonflower Murders is a deviously dark take on vintage English crime fiction in which the reader becomes the detective.

book.title: The Vanishing Hour
book.description: In the rain-soaked streets of Blackwood Falls, people are disappearing—not all at once, but one by one, always at the same hour: 3:17 AM. No signs of struggle. No traces left behind. Just an empty bed, a cold cup of coffee, and a silence that screams louder than any cry for help. Detective Mara Voss has spent seven years running from her own ghosts. When a string of impossible vanishings pulls her back to the town she swore never to return to, she discovers that the disappearances are connected by something far more terrifying than a serial killer. The victims all share one thing in common—they each received a letter. A letter that arrived exactly seven days before they vanished. A letter written in handwriting that matches Mara's own. As the clock ticks toward the next vanishing hour, Mara must confront the darkest corners of her past, unravel a conspiracy that reaches into the town's founding, and face a truth so unsettling it will make her question the nature of reality itself. The Vanishing Hour is a gripping psychological thriller that explores memory, guilt, and the secrets we bury so deep they begin to bury us. With atmospheric prose, relentless tension, and a twist that will leave readers breathless, Peter Ickes delivers a debut novel that lingers long after the final page.

book.title: The Puzzle Killer
book.description: The Puzzle Killer is a brilliantly crafted psychological crime thriller where every murder is a piece of an impossible puzzle, every clue is deliberately misleading, and solving the mystery may require sacrificing the detective's own sanity. When renowned cryptographer Professor Nathan Reeves is found murdered inside a locked observatory, investigators discover an elaborate wooden puzzle box resting beside the body. Inside is a single handwritten message: "The first piece is never the beginning." Detective Isabella Cross, one of the country's most gifted homicide investigators, is assigned what appears to be an isolated ritualistic killing. But before the victim's identity can even be officially released, another body is discovered hundreds of miles away—accompanied by an identical puzzle, another impossible crime scene, and another cryptic message. As the murders escalate, Isabella realizes she is chasing a killer who doesn't leave fingerprints, weapons, or conventional evidence. Instead, each crime is meticulously staged as one fragment of a much larger intellectual game. Ancient ciphers, mathematical sequences, impossible mazes, chess strategies, optical illusions, and mechanical puzzles become the only language the murderer is willing to speak. Joining forces with FBI behavioral analyst Dr. Adrian Cole and puzzle historian Emma Sinclair, Isabella uncovers evidence linking the victims to a forgotten government-funded research project that explored the psychology of genius, obsession, and pattern recognition. Decades earlier, a small group of exceptional children participated in experimental cognitive testing. Only one disappeared without explanation. Now someone has returned to finish the final puzzle. Every new victim reveals another hidden piece of an intricate design stretching back more than thirty years. Encrypted diaries, abandoned laboratories, coded museum exhibits, and impossible escape rooms conceal clues that point toward an invisible mastermind capable of predicting every investigative move before it happens. With each solution, the detectives unknowingly trigger the next murder, forcing Isabella to confront a terrifying possibility: The killer isn't trying to escape. The killer is designing the investigation. As public panic spreads and law enforcement struggles to stay ahead, Isabella becomes the final piece in a deadly game where failure means more than another murder—it means allowing a lifetime of manipulation to reach its perfectly engineered conclusion. The breathtaking finale unfolds inside a forgotten underground complex built entirely as a living puzzle, where every decision changes the outcome and every answer raises one final question: Can justice exist if the truth itself has been designed as a trap? Blending psychological suspense, classic detective fiction, cryptography, forensic investigation, and relentless twists, The Puzzle Killer delivers an unforgettable reading experience filled with brilliant mysteries, emotionally compelling characters, and a climax that rewards readers who pay attention to every detail. Perfect for fans of Alex Michaelides, Anthony Horowitz, Keigo Higashino, Jeffery Deaver, and Peter Swanson, The Puzzle Killer is an intelligent page-turner that asks one chilling question: What if the only way to catch a serial killer was to become the final piece of the puzzle?

book.description: 'A must-read for murder mystery lovers' DAILY MAIL 'Ellis conjures up an immersive, authentic world in this evocative series' FINANCIAL TIMES 'Gripping...expertly combining a crime mystery with a wartime thriller....a potent mix which has produced this excellent novel' ALEX GERLIS ***AN ASPECTS OF CRIME BOOK OF THE YEAR*** WINNER OF THE 2026 COB AND PEN LITERARY AWARD*** London. book.title: The Hopepunk Manifesto
book.description:
Hope is not a feeling. It is a practice.

In a world of climate crisis, political polarization, and pervasive despair, hope has been dismissed as naive, weak, or worse — a luxury for those who can afford to ignore reality. The Hopepunk Manifesto rejects that lie.

Part cultural criticism, part story collection, this book defines hopepunk — the literary and philosophical movement that began with a single Tumblr post in 2017 and has since grown into a global community of writers, artists, and activists — and demonstrates its power through original short fiction.

Through five manifesto essays and five stories, you will discover:

·        Why hope is a discipline, not a feeling

·        How despair is used as a tool of oppression

·        Why community is essential to resistance

·        The craft principles behind hopepunk storytelling

·        Daily practices for living optimistic resistance

You will meet gardeners and radio operators, repairers and space travelers, organizers and dreamers. You will see hope tested, failed, and chosen again. You will see what it looks like to build a better world — not with a single hero, but with a community.

For readers of Becky Chambers, Kim Stanley Robinson, Rebecca Solnit, and adrienne maree brown, The Hopepunk Manifesto is an invitation to join a movement that is already underway.

The world is broken. Let's fix it together.

book.title: The Desert Talon
book.description:
Sephihalé ele Janan sits in a prison cell in the southern island of Mazemoor, dreaming of escape. After months in a provisional prison for fighting for the imperial Kattakans, Janan is sponsored by another refugee who was once a part of his scattered family. Yearning to build a life on his sister's land with the dragons their people revere, the peace Janan seeks is threatened by a ruthless dragon baron who covets both Janan's connection to the earth and the battle dragon to which he is covenanted.

The conflict may drive Janan to acts of violence he hoped to leave behind in the war, and bring more death to the land Janan now calls home.

The Desert Talon is a story of two groups of people who, despite a common ancestry, have diverged so far in their beliefs that there appears to be little mutual ground - and the conflict may well start to unravel the burgeoning hopes of a country, and a man, still recovering from the ravages of war.

catalogueCheck.description:
Classic crime fiction's 'Indiana Jones' Tony Medawar unearths more unpublished and uncollected stories from the Golden Age of suspense, including John Bude, John Dickson Carr, Dorothy L. Sayers and Julian Symons.

‘Five books in, and the selection here might well be the strongest yet. This series continues to delight with the high standard of forgotten gems that Medawar uncovers, and there’s sufficient range to ensure that all fans of the genre will find something to enjoy. Book 6 can’t come soon enough.’
Jim Noy, author of The Red Death Murders

The end of the First World War saw the rise of an insatiable public appetite for clever and thrilling mystery fiction and a new kind of hero – the modern crime writer. As the genre soared in popularity, so did the inventiveness of its best authors, ushering in a “Golden Age” of detective fiction – two decades of exemplary mystery writing: the era of the whodunit, the impossible crime and the locked-room mystery, with stories that have thrilled and baffled generations of readers.

The Golden Age still casts a long shadow, with many of the authors who were published at that time still hugely popular today. Aside from novels, they all wrote short fiction – stories, serials and plays – and although many have been republished in books over the last 100 years, Bodies from the Library collects the ones that are impossible to find: stories that appeared in a newspaper, magazine or an anthology that has long been out of print; ephemeral works such as plays not aired, staged or screened for decades; and unpublished stories that were absorbed into an author’s archive when they died . . .

Complete with fascinating biographies by Tony Medawar of all the featured authors, this latest volume in the annual Bodies from the Library series once again brings into the daylight the forgotten, the lost and the unknown, and is an indispensable collection for any bookshelf.

In the fog-shrouded coastal town of Ashmere Bay, Detective Clara Voss thought she had left her demons behind. Transferred from the bustling precinct of New York to what seemed like a quiet retirement post, Clara expected nothing more than petty thefts and neighborhood disputes.


But when a young woman vanishes without a trace from the town's annual Harvest Festival, Clara is thrust into an investigation that unearths decades of buried secrets.


As more people disappear under eerily similar circumstances, Clara discovers a chilling pattern: every victim was last seen near the old lighthouse on Blackwood Point, and every disappearance happened exactly twenty years apart.


The town's elders know more than they're saying, the local historian guards a dangerous truth, and the lighthouse keeper who vanished in 1984 may hold the key to everything.


The Last Echo is a gripping psychological thriller that weaves together past and present, exploring how the sins of one generation echo through the next. Perfect for fans of atmospheric mysteries, small-town thrillers, and character-driven suspense.

In the quiet English village of Bellgrave, the morning light has always been considered sacred.

For generations, villagers have gathered on the hill overlooking the valley to watch the sunrise.

But beneath that hill lies a secret that has remained buried for more than a century.

In 1912, a group of villagers disappeared without explanation.

Their homes were abandoned.

Their names were erased from local records.

And a strange stone was placed beneath the hill where they were last seen.

No one ever discovered why.

More than a hundred years later, Clara Whitmore, a young historian investigating forgotten wartime records, arrives in Bellgrave.

She expects to uncover an old historical mystery.

Instead, she discovers a hidden journal containing a warning:

“Never dig beneath the morning light.”

Clara initially assumes the warning is superstition.

Until she finds the first grave.

There is no body inside.

Only an ancient silver key.

After Clara touches it, strange things begin happening.

She dreams about people who lived in Bellgrave more than a century ago.

She hears footsteps in rooms that have been empty for decades.

Old photographs begin changing.

And every morning at sunrise, a mysterious figure appears on the hill.

Clara soon realizes that the disappearance of the villagers in 1912 was not a historical accident.

They discovered something buried beneath the hill.

Something ancient.

Something that should never have been awakened.

And now that Clara has found the key, whatever was buried beneath Bellgrave knows that someone has finally come looking.

book.title: Beneath the City of Silent Clocks
book.description: In the city of Velmara, every clock stopped at exactly 11:47 on a cold November night — and never started again. Fifty years later, the townsfolk have learned to live with The Stillness, the catastrophe that silenced their once-famous clockmaking capital. But twenty-four-year-old Elara Voss, the last apprentice of the city's final Master Clockmaker, begins to hear something impossible: the faint, steady ticking of a clock beneath the floor of her workshop. What she finds underneath will change everything she thought she knew. Beneath the streets of Velmara lies the Undercroft — a vast, ancient mechanism older than the city itself, built by a forgotten civilization to hold time in place. For five decades, it has been maintained in secret by her mentor, Silas Thorne, a man who has sacrificed everything to keep its rings turning and its terrible purpose fulfilled. But the mechanism is failing. And the clocks are not broken — they are holding something back. When journalist Marcus Chen arrives in Velmara searching for his missing sister, and detective Iris Hale uncovers a pattern of disappearances stretching back decades, Elara is drawn into a conspiracy far older and far darker than she ever imagined. Together, they must descend into the labyrinth beneath the city, where the truth about The Stillness — and about Elara's own mother's death — has been waiting in the dark. What the Undercroft contains is not a catastrophe. It is a choice. And the time to make it is running out. A gripping literary mystery about memory, obsession, and the price of trying to outrun time itself, Beneath the City of Silent Clocks will keep you turning pages long past your own bedtime.

Perhaps he always has. In his notebooks, day after day, he makes a clear and careful record of its wonders: the labyrinth of halls, the thousands upon thousands of statues, the tides that thunder up staircases, the clouds that move in slow procession through the upper halls. On Tuesdays and Fridays Piranesi sees his friend, the Other. At other times he brings tributes of food to the Dead. But mostly, he is alone. Messages begin to appear, scratched out in chalk on the pavements. There is someone new in the House. But who are they and what do they want?
